title: UK: Hawkish Monetary Policy Committee puts a December hike on the table
gist: Oxford Economics says the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate 25bps to 4% with more hawkish messaging, driven by higher energy futures and domestic resilience that raise second-round inflation risk. Another hike in December or February is likely, with December a coin flip hinging on oil and natural gas prices; the house view keeps a 4.25% peak because it expects limited second-round effects on pay and margins, but flags upside risks.

themes.theme: MPC hike to 4% and hawkish shift

insights.claim: The UK Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate by 25bps to 4% at its early-November 2026 meeting, and its messaging was more hawkish than at previous meetings.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: UK policy is in an active tightening phase with a hawkish bias; front-end gilt pricing should not assume an imminent pause.
insights.quote: The Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate by 25bps to 4% on Thursday.
insights.locator: The Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate

insights.claim: Higher energy futures prices and further evidence of domestic economic resilience are both raising the risk that second-round inflation effects emerge in the UK.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: An energy shock combined with a resilient domestic economy is the combination that pushes the BoE toward further hikes rather than looking through supply-driven inflation.
insights.quote: Higher energy futures prices and more evidence of domestic resilience both increase the risk of second-round effects emerging.
insights.locator: The committee's messaging was more hawkish

insights.claim: Oxford Economics judges that the inflationary pressure already in the UK system makes another Bank Rate hike likely, either in December or February.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: At least one more 25bp hike to 4.25% is the base case; the debate is timing, not direction.
insights.quote: The degree of inflationary pressure already in the system means another hike is likely, in December or February.
insights.locator: The committee's messaging was more hawkish

insights.claim: Whether the MPC hikes again in December is roughly a 50/50 call, with the path of oil and natural gas prices set to be the decisive factor.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Oil and gas price moves over the coming weeks are the key signal for December BoE pricing; energy prices effectively act as the trigger for UK rate timing.
insights.quote: December’s meeting now looks like a coin flip, with the path of oil and natural gas prices set to be the decisive factor
insights.locator: The Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate

themes.theme: Terminal rate view and upside risk

insights.claim: The MPC majority signalled that once Bank Rate reaches 4.25%, subsequent rate decisions will become a closer call, implying a higher bar for tightening beyond that level.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: 4.25% is the natural focal point for the terminal rate; pricing of hikes beyond it depends on fresh evidence rather than momentum.
insights.quote: The majority gave the impression that once Bank Rate reaches 4.25%, subsequent decisions will be a closer call.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics maintains its forecast that UK Bank Rate will peak at 4.25%, because it expects second-round effects on pay and margins to prove limited, while acknowledging risks to that peak are skewed to the upside.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: The call for a 4.25% peak relies on wages and margins staying contained; strong pay or margin data would point to a higher terminal rate.
insights.quote: we maintain our forecast that Bank Rate will peak at 4.25%, but the risks are skewed to the upside
